bug_description.original: Detailed Report: https://oss-fuzz.com/testcase?key=5643281198481408 Project: leptonica Fuzzing Engine: afl Fuzz Target: barcode_fuzzer Job Type: afl_asan_leptonica Platform Id: linux Crash Type: Heap-use-after-free READ 1 Crash Address: 0x61d0000025d7 Crash State: pixAverageRasterScans pixExtractBarcodeCrossings pixExtractBarcodeWidths1 Sanitizer: address (ASAN) Recommended Security Severity: High Regressed: https://oss-fuzz.com/revisions?job=afl_asan_leptonica&range=202005020213:202005030215 Reproducer Testcase: https://oss-fuzz.com/download?testcase_id=5643281198481408 Issue filed automatically.
bug_description.normalized: The staged witness is a serialized SPIX image that decodes to a 75x32 1 bpp PIX and reaches Leptonica's barcode-width extraction path. In the vulnerable source, pixReadBarcodes forwards an attacker-derived deskewed barcode crop into pixExtractBarcodeCrossings without checking that the crop is tall enough for the fixed 51-scan averaging window. pixAverageRasterScans then reads the crop height and applies the inverted guard `if (nscans <= h)` instead of clamping when `nscans > h`. On the crashing call, that leaves `nscans = 51` on a shorter barcode crop, computes `first = (h - 51) / 2` and `last = first + 50`, and thereby guarantees `last > h - 1` for any `h < 51` (with `first < 0` only when `h <= 49`) before iterating `GET_DATA_BYTE(line, j)` on rows outside the barcode buffer. In the reproduced run, the out-of-range address falls inside the heap region of a temporary edge-filter PIX already freed by pixLocateBarcodes, so AddressSanitizer reports heap-use-after-free at readbarcode.c:805.

source.description: First project-side read of attacker-controlled image geometry from the SPIX buffer. These statements materialize the witness as a 75x32, 1 bpp image whose pixels later enter barcode processing.
source.value_from: The staged 412-byte `poc` begins with SPIX magic `spix` and little-endian header words `w = 75`, `h = 32`, `d = 1`, `ncolors = 0`, `imdata_size = 384`.

tainted_value_origin.description: Attacker-derived barcode pixels are deskewed and cropped into `pixt`. When the subsequent confidence test accepts it, this crop is retained and later becomes the `pixs` argument to pixAverageRasterScans.

root_cause.description: The clamp predicate is reversed. When the requested scan count exceeds the crop height, the code should reset `nscans` to `h`, but this condition instead takes the out-of-range path and leaves `nscans` larger than the image.

sink.description: The raster-averaging loop reads a byte through `line = data + i * wpl` after the scan window is derived so that `last > h - 1` and at least one loop iteration indexes beyond the valid row range. AddressSanitizer reports that this 1-byte read lands in the heap region of a temporary PIX that was already freed at pixLocateBarcodes:412.

parser_admitted.description: The witness passes the SPIX magic check and the size/dimension sanity checks in pixDeserializeFromMemory, so Leptonica admits the input as an image and returns a PIX to the barcode path.

coarse_trace.summary: Leptonica parses the attacker-controlled SPIX buffer into a small 75x32 image and materializes its raster data.
Barcode processing converts the image to 8 bpp, deskews and crops a candidate barcode, and retains the resulting barcode PIX in the output pixa.
The retained barcode crop is passed into the width-decoding path without a minimum-size guard, reaching pixExtractBarcodeCrossings with a fixed 51-scan request.

pixAverageRasterScans mis-handles the short barcode crop with the inverted `nscans <= h` test, derives out-of-range row bounds, and reads outside the crop buffer; the accessed byte lies in a previously freed temporary PIX allocation, producing the saved ASan heap-use-after-free report.

fine_trace.note: Reads attacker-controlled SPIX header fields and materializes the witness image geometry as `w = 75`, `h = 32`, `d = 1`.
Allocates the 75x32, 1 bpp PIX and copies the 384-byte attacker-controlled raster into it, creating the concrete `pixs` object consumed by the barcode code.
Barcode processing requires 8 bpp input. Because the witness image has `d = 1`, the false branch runs and creates an 8 bpp `pixg` from the attacker-controlled PIX.
Creates the attacker-derived deskewed barcode crop `pixt` and retains it in `pixa` when the confidence test succeeds. The later read path proves at least one crop passes this gate.

fine_trace.code:
pixt = pixaGetPix(pixa, i, L_CLONE);
na = pixReadBarcodeWidths(pixt, method, debugflag);
fine_trace.note: Clones the retained barcode crop and immediately feeds it into barcode-width extraction. The vulnerable source performs no minimum-size check here; the fix later inserts `pixGetDimensions(pixt, &w, &h, NULL)` and skips crops with `w < 100 || h < 50` before this call.
The width-based decode path reaches raster averaging with a fixed request for 51 centered scan lines on the cloned barcode crop.

Loads the current barcode-crop geometry. The reproduced crash inside this function implies the active crop height satisfies `h < 51`; otherwise the subsequent branch would clamp the scan range to valid rows and line 805 would stay in bounds.
Root cause. With `nscans = 51` and `h < 51`, this inverted test is false, so the function takes the `else` path instead of clamping `nscans` down to `h` for a short image.

Because the short-image case wrongly fell into the `else` branch, the centered scan window is derived with `nscans` still larger than `h`. This computes `first = (h - 51) / 2` and `last = first + 50`; for every `h < 51`, `last > h - 1`, so the loop is guaranteed to visit rows past the crop, while `first < 0` only when `h <= 49`.

Sink. The loop uses `i` values from the out-of-range window in step 9 to compute `line = data + i * wpl`, and `GET_DATA_BYTE(line, j)` reads 1 byte from invalid memory. The source-level arithmetic guarantees some `i > h - 1`, and `i < 0` also occurs when `h <= 49`. The saved ASan trace reports that the accessed address belongs to the temporary edge-filter PIX region freed earlier by `pixDestroy(&pixe)` in `pixLocateBarcodes` line 412, yielding heap-use-after-free.

evidence_limitations: The saved artifacts do not record the exact deskewed barcode-crop dimensions or which orientation arm inside pixDeskewBarcode was taken. With `runtime_disambiguation` disabled, this GT records only the source-grounded fact needed to close the chain: the crashing call to pixAverageRasterScans had `h < 51`, because otherwise the branch at line 788 would clamp the scan window and line 805 would not read out of range.

allocation_context.description: ASan attributes the later invalid read address to the `pixd = pixCreateTemplate(pixs);` allocation for the temporary edge-filter PIX used inside pixLocateBarcodes during barcode deskew.

free_context.description: The same temporary edge-filter PIX is freed by `pixDestroy(&pixe);` immediately after thresholding.

format.name: SPIX serialized 75x32 1 bpp image
format.contract: The staged 412-byte SPIX witness must decode to `w = 75`, `h = 32`, `d = 1`, `ncolors = 0` and drive barcode processing far enough that a retained deskewed barcode crop reaches `pixAverageRasterScans(pixs, 51)` with `h < 51`, so the inverted `if (nscans <= h)` test computes out-of-range scan rows and line 805 reads outside the crop.
